raw_response:
I farm only 1.5 mu, so I count every bag and every yuan carefully. I have done this for many years, so I do not start from zero. I start from what worked before and then I adjust a little. For maize here, I will still use hybrid seed, because the local hybrids usually stand better and give more grain than the old seed. On such a small plot, if I save a little on seed but lose yield, that is not worth it. I have well water, so I am less afraid of dry spells, and that lets me push fertilizer a bit more. I will put most of the fertilizer in as base fertilizer and then add nitrogen once more when the maize is growing fast. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than watch the cobs stay small. I will not go too fancy, because my land is small and family labor is limited, but I will keep the field clean, water it at the key times, and spray when I see real pest pressure. Around here, if maize is managed steadily with water and fertilizer, the yield can still be decent on small land. I will use rotary tillage because it is easier and cheaper for my size than deep ploughing, and it is what many people nearby do.
